`catalog-info.yaml` has two errors, and either one will make Backstage reject the entity. I didn't change any files.

I opened the file and ran the skill's structural checker on it, which exited with code 1:

```
catalog-info.yaml:4: error: invalid metadata.name 'Ledger Sync!': ...
catalog-info.yaml:1: error: Component requires spec.owner
Checked 1 file(s), 1 document(s): 2 error(s), 0 warning(s).
```

**1. The name is invalid (`catalog-info.yaml:4`)**
`metadata.name: Ledger Sync!` breaks Backstage's default naming rules. Names can only contain letters and digits, separated by single `-`, `_` or `.` characters, and can't start or end with a separator. The space and the `!` aren't allowed.
- **Suggested fix:** `name: ledger-sync`. The README heading is `# ledger-sync`. If you want to keep the readable form, put `Ledger Sync` in `metadata.title`.

**2. `spec.owner` is missing (`catalog-info.yaml:1`)**
Every Component must have an owner, and this one has none.
- **Open question:** the repository has no CODEOWNERS file or other ownership information. I can't suggest an owner, so you'll need to supply the real group or user reference, for example `group:<team-name>`.

**Minor (not an error)**
- There are no annotations, such as `github.com/project-slug`, and no links. Without a source-control slug, the CI, source and docs plugins won't be able to find the repository. I didn't find the repository's remote URL here, so I can't suggest a value.

**Fields that are fine:** `apiVersion`, `kind: Component`, `description`, `spec.type: service` and `spec.lifecycle: production` are all well formed. I found nothing to contradict `production`, but nothing confirms it either.

The checker only looks at structure. I didn't run Backstage's own validation (`validate-entity` or a location dry run) because there was no Backstage instance to send it to. Once both errors are fixed, run that before registering the file.
